pulserver.pypulseq.Sequence#

class pulserver.pypulseq.Sequence#

Sequence container tuned for append-only generation, with extensions.

A drop-in subclass of pypulseq.Sequence for the case a plugin actually has: blocks are emitted strictly in order and never revisited. On that assumption the per-block deduplication and gradient-continuity checks are skipped and each add_block becomes a direct library insertion — which is what keeps generation tractable for sequences with hundreds of thousands of blocks. Deduplication still happens, once, at write.

It also accepts the extension events upstream does not: user-defined labels (make_label()), block rotations (make_rotation()), and pTx shim vectors (make_rf_shim()).

Because blocks are never re-checked, this class assumes you append in order. Use pypulseq.Sequence if you need to modify blocks after adding them.

Parameters:

  • system (pypulseq.Opts, optional) – System limits recorded in the .seq header.

  • use_block_cache (bool, optional) – Kept for upstream compatibility; off by default.

Examples

>>> import pulserver.pypulseq as pp
>>> seq = pp.Sequence(pp.Opts())
>>> seq.add_block(pp.make_delay(1e-3), pp.make_label("LIN", "SET", 0))
>>> len(seq.block_events)
1

Append modules rather than events, and write at the end:

for ky in range(ny):
    excitation(seq)
    readout(seq, pe_idx=ky)
seq.write(output_path)

See also

make_label, make_rotation, make_rf_shim

__init__(system=None, use_block_cache=False)#
add_block(*args)#

Append a block assuming strictly sequential insertion.

calculate_kspace(*, tr_index=None, segment=None, **kwargs)#

k-space trajectory of the sequence, or of one TR / segment.

Upstream’s trajectory calculation has no time-range argument, so a scoped call runs against a sliced copy of the plotting view.

check_timing(print_errors=False)#

Run upstream’s timing check against the plotting view.

duration()#

Total duration, block count and event count of the sequence.

get_block(block_index)#

Decode one block through the plain view.

The block libraries of the fast builder are write-only, so this goes through _seq. Extensions are not part of the returned block; read them from extensions.

grad_spectrum(*, tr_index=None, segment=None, bands=None, esp_file=None, asc_file=None, window_width=None, max_frequency=2000.0, plot=True, **kwargs)#

Gradient spectrum, with mechanical resonance bands overlaid.

This is a visualisation only — whether a sequence clears a forbidden band is decided by the C safety core at predownload, not here.

Parameters:

  • tr_index (int, optional) – Restrict the analysis to one TR or segment. When tr_index is given and window_width is not, the window is set to the whole TR, so the result is one spectrum rather than a spectrogram.

  • segment (int, optional) – Restrict the analysis to one TR or segment. When tr_index is given and window_width is not, the window is set to the whole TR, so the result is one spectrum rather than a spectrogram.

  • bands (list of tuple, optional) – Forbidden bands as (freq_min_hz, freq_max_hz, max_amplitude_mT_per_m[, channel]). Defaults to system.forbidden_bands when the sequence’s Opts carries them.

  • esp_file (str or pathlib.Path, optional) – Read the bands from a GE ESP lockout table instead. See read_esp_bands().

  • asc_file (str or pathlib.Path, optional) – Read the bands from a Siemens .asc file instead. See read_asc_bands().

  • window_width (float, optional) – Analysis window in seconds.

  • max_frequency (float, default 2000.0) – Upper frequency limit of the spectrum.

  • plot (bool, default True) – Draw the spectrogram.

Returns:

tuple – (spectrograms, spectrogram_sos, frequencies, times), as pypulseq.Sequence.calculate_gradient_spectrum() returns.

payload()#

Serialise this sequence to the .seq payload the views are built from.

Deduplicated, exactly as pulserver.io.write() would emit it — the C backend requires canonical event IDs to recognise repeated RF shims and gradients across TRs, and the views should show what is actually going to be written.

plot(*, tr_index=None, segment=None, **kwargs)#

Plot the sequence as the scanner plays it.

Rotations and RF shims are resolved into the waveforms (see _seqplot), so a rotated readout is drawn on the axes it will actually run on and a pTx pulse shows one trace per transmit channel.

Parameters:

  • tr_index (int, optional) – Restrict the plot to one TR. Mutually exclusive with segment.

  • segment (int, optional) – Restrict the plot to one segment’s max-energy instance.

  • **kwargs – Passed through to pypulseq.Sequence.plot(); time_range is set for you when a scope is given.

plot_kspace(*, tr_index=None, segment=None, plot_now=True, **kwargs)#

Plot the k-space trajectory, with ADC sample locations marked.

Parameters:

  • tr_index (int, optional) – Restrict to one TR or segment.

  • segment (int, optional) – Restrict to one TR or segment.

  • plot_now (bool, default True) – Show the figure immediately.

  • **kwargs – Passed to calculate_kspace().

Returns:

matplotlib.figure.Figure

pns(*, tr_index=None, segment=None, model='chronaxie', chronaxie_us=None, rheobase=None, alpha=None, hardware=None, thresholds=(80.0, 100.0), plot=True)#

Peripheral nerve stimulation response, for inspection only.

Two nerve models are available. 'chronaxie' is the Irnich rheobase/chronaxie form GE uses, and is the same arithmetic the interpreter runs at predownload. 'safe' delegates to upstream’s SAFE implementation, which needs Siemens hardware parameters.

No verdict is returned: the threshold lines are drawn so the margin is visible, and the pass/fail decision stays with the C safety core.

Parameters:

  • tr_index (int, optional) – Restrict the analysis to one TR or segment.

  • segment (int, optional) – Restrict the analysis to one TR or segment.

  • model ({'chronaxie', 'safe'}, default 'chronaxie') – Nerve model to use.

  • chronaxie_us (float, optional) – Irnich model parameters. Default to the matching attributes of the sequence’s Opts when it carries them (pulserver.pypulseq.Opts does).

  • rheobase (float, optional) – Irnich model parameters. Default to the matching attributes of the sequence’s Opts when it carries them (pulserver.pypulseq.Opts does).

  • alpha (float, optional) – Irnich model parameters. Default to the matching attributes of the sequence’s Opts when it carries them (pulserver.pypulseq.Opts does).

  • hardware (optional) – SAFE hardware description or Siemens .asc path, for model='safe'. Defaults to system.pns_hardware when the sequence’s Opts carries one.

  • thresholds (sequence of float, default (80.0, 100.0)) – Percentage lines to draw.

  • plot (bool, default True) – Draw the result.

Returns:

tuple – (pns_percent, t) where pns_percent has shape (N, 3).

read(*_args, **_kwargs)#

Fast builder does not support reading/parsing external sequence files.

remove_duplicates(in_place=False)#

Remove duplicates with hardcoded rounded profiles per library.

Unlike upstream pypulseq, this also compacts extension-related libraries and canonicalizes extension linked lists so identical chains are shared across blocks.

Parameters:

in_place – If True, deduplicate current instance; otherwise return a copy.

rf_from_lib_data(lib_data, use='')#

Decode RF use from numeric code (fast path) or legacy char.

segment(index)#

Return one Segment by index.

set_block(_block_index, *args)#

Disable positional insertion/update in fast mode.

test_report()#

Upstream’s textual sequence report.

tr_block_range(tr_index)#

Inclusive 1-based block range of TR tr_index.

The TR layout comes from the C library, so a plugin does not have to declare it — whatever structure the blocks actually have is what gets indexed.

waveforms(*, tr_index=None, segment=None, append_RF=False)#

Uniformly sampled waveforms, optionally restricted to a TR or segment.

waveforms_and_times(append_RF=False)#

Event waveforms with their time stamps, from the plotting view.

write(name, create_signature=False, remove_duplicates=False, check_timing=False, v141_compat=False)#

Fast builder does not support writing sequence files.

property custom_labels#

Labels auto-registered beyond the built-in get_supported_labels() set.

Maps label_string -> int_idx for every custom label encountered via add_block(). The custom write helper uses this to serialise them.

property extensions#

Block extensions, keyed by 1-based block index.

See pulserver.pypulseq._extensions.BlockExtensions.

property num_trs#

Number of TRs detected in the sequence.

property segments#

Every virtual segment, resolved to its max-energy instance.

Segmentation is the C library’s, so this is the same partitioning the scanner executes and the safety backend analyses.

property tr_duration#

Detected TR duration in seconds.

property tr_info#

TR structure of the sequence as detected by the C backend.

Returns:

dict – Keys include tr_size (blocks per TR), num_trs, num_prep_blocks, tr_duration_us and num_canonical_trs.
